page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage is provided via a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 24294.54 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 8497.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 934.0 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.34 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small blocks at 946.78 GB/sec, but drops to 150.22 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated CPU allocation support steady database operations, scoring 10377.61 on Passmark database benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a high physical core density without simultaneous multithreading, offering predictable performance per resource. However, workloads requiring advanced vector extensions or high single-threaded performance may experience limitations. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded compute workloads, local database hosting, static web serving, and software compilation.
